sources.title: Value Added Tax (Amendment of Schedules) Regulations, 2014 (S.I. 4 of 2014, made under section 52(1) of the Value Added Tax Act, Act 35 of 2010) — repeals and replaces the Schedules: First Schedule Part II (exempt supplies, items 1 to 5), Second Schedule (zero-rated supplies), Third Schedule (rate of VAT, 15 %), Fourth Schedule (registration threshold, SCR 3,000,000 in this text)
sources.publisher: Minister of Finance, Trade and Investment (Supplement to the Official Gazette, 20 January 2014; copy hosted by the World Trade Organization)

sources.title: Seychelles Revenue Commission — Value Added Tax Return: lines 1 to 11, columns A (value) and B (VAT), with the instructions for completing it; the return is lodged with the Business Activity Statement by the 21st of the month following the taxable period

Revenue Law (Amendment) Act 2023 (Act 27 of 2023, Supplement to the Official Gazette, 22 December 2023) — new section 3(1) and (2) of the Revenue Administration Act: a monthly return is furnished by the 21st day of the month when furnished in person and by the 23rd when furnished through the SRC Tax Portal, and a large business furnishes through the Portal; new section 20: the monthly tax is paid by the 21st in person and by the 23rd through the Portal or by bank transfer, and a payment of SCR 50,000 or more goes through the Portal

What is Value Added Tax (VAT)? — information brochure: standard rate 15 %, zero-rated supplies (mainly exports) as taxable supplies at 0 % with input tax deductible, exempt supplies with no right to deduct

SRC guidance on the amendments made to the Fourth Schedule of the VAT Act 2010 (S.I. 97 of 2024): compulsory registration at SCR 2,000,000 of taxable supplies, voluntary registration from SCR 100,000, application within 14 days
Business Activity Statement — the form on which the VAT due (box 10A of the return) is paid, with the other monthly taxes; due by the 21st day of the month following

IAS 1 Presentation of Financial Statements — the statement of financial position and the statement of profit or loss, expenses analysed by nature; no Seychelles text prescribing a layout or a chart of accounts was found
Seychelles Revenue Commission — tax administration portal (forms, guidance, Tax Portal for returns and payments)

charts.name: Seychelles reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in the texts read for Seychelles, and no text prescribing a financial reporting framework was found (see the README). This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IFRS-style statements below (IAS 1, expenses by nature), with the accounts a Seychelles trading company keeps — VAT output and input tax, import VAT owed to the Seychelles Revenue Commission at the border, Income and Non-Monetary Benefits Tax withheld, social security contributions, and the Tourism Marketing Tax.

einvoicing.legal_reference: No structured e-invoice standard, Peppol profile or clearance system of the Seychelles Revenue Commission was found in the texts read; the Tax Portal takes the returns and payments, not invoices. `obligation` is `none` for want of a text, not on a finding that none exists.

not_taxed.legal_reference: The texts read — the Schedules of 2014, the VAT return, the Commission's brochures — contain no rule making the buyer in Seychelles assess the tax on a service bought from a supplier abroad: the return has no line for it, and the brochure says VAT is collected at Customs on imports and at the point of sale. The pack therefore carries no purchase tax for it. This is a finding about the texts read, not about the Act, which was not found; if the Act has a reverse charge, it is a gap recorded in the README.
